The opinion's own limiting language says the case relates only to seizure of contraband known before arrest.
The disclosed files do not include any SIA Persons page or role standard that would verify the 'origin' label.

reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tie the home role to the actual supported contribution: historical warrant-practicability rule for a foreseeable property seizure incident to arrest.

defect.evidence_quote: Rather the test is the apparent need for summary seizure
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the wording is slightly overbroad unless limited to the facts the Court emphasized: known contraband, known location/nature, ample opportunity for a warrant, and no apparent need for summary seizure.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: 'Where officers knew the existence, nature, and location of the contraband long before a lawful arrest, had abundant time to get a search warrant, and no apparent need for summary seizure existed, Trupiano required them to obtain a warrant before seizing the contraband under its whenever-reasonably-practicable rule.'

reasons: The text supports the lawful-arrest premise: the Court sustained Antoniole's warrantless arrest.
The text supports the warrant rule: officers must secure and use search warrants wherever reasonably practicable.
The text supports suppression of the seizure because agents knew the distillery details long before the raid and had abundant time to get a warrant.
The later Rabinowitz/Chimel clause is treatment/currency and is not assessed under Lens A.
residual_risks: The lake record has no pinpoints or progeny edges, so later-treatment components remain for Lens B.
